chrome: signed Google stable 158.0.8127.37, original macOS arm64 receipts
scope: Only previously collected v2 eligible observations. No browser runs, no input replay and no product edits. Ranking is a shortlist, not an exhaustive attribution of the gap.
rankingRules: Rows are ranked by distinct Chrome-only occurrences (URL, canonical name, occurrence), with an independent practical priority order. A row is assigned to at most one ranked family. Pages may span families and strict-page bounds must not be summed.

Direct named prerequisite counts use original named diagnostics naming the missing binding/operation or unsupported algorithm family, including wrong exceptions from an unsupported primitive. They show the first observed blocker, not guaranteed gains. Page setup counts use the page error when the name is absent. Other rows are file/name-correlated, including cases without diagnostic evidence and timeout/not-run statuses.

Strict page bound counts use matched current/Chrome page sets. An otherwise-strict page is Chrome-strict, currently complete/OK, nonempty, and every currently reported nonpassing name is in that family. Correcting the upstream blocker can reveal new names or failures.

The paint family includes only rows with an explicit missing canvas.requestPaint diagnostic, and not arbitrary canvas pixel mismatches. Crypto family assignment prioritizes hybrid labels, then ML-KEM and ML-DSA file/name labels. Unlabeled shared modern-algorithm cases are left unassigned.

webnnDeviceCaveat: CPU/GPU/NPU query strings are requested context variants, not independent proof that the corresponding hardware executed. Observed signed required/optional operation names arise after supported-feature filtering and actual expected tensor output comparison. No backend/device counters were present in these receipts; context registration or fallback alone cannot claim numerical parity.
practicalPriorityRationale: Start bounded browser API work with Cookie Store and the Origin value API. Library-backend review for ML-KEM/ML-DSA can proceed independently with known-answer and usage/format controls. Keep WebNN and WebGL as separate subsystem feasibility decisions, and coordinate canvas or media changes with the relevant owner.
